video.title: Task, Executor & Cooperative Thread Pool | Day 259
video.description:
Learn to explain where async work runs and who decides: Task, Executor & Cooperative Thread Pool, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Task - A unit of `async` work that runs on its own and can be awaited for its result.
Executor - An object that decides where and when a task's code runs, such as a queue or a thread.
Cooperative Thread Pool - A small, fixed group of threads that Swift shares among all `async` work.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Task, Executor and Cooperative Thread Pool in English?

dialogue.title: Where does it run?
dialogue.setting: Questions about where async work runs

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I wrote a Task, but I do not know when it runs.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A Task is a unit of async work. It starts on its own, and you can await its result.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That depends on the executor. An executor decides where and when the code runs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Is an executor the same as a thread?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. It can be a queue or a thread. Swift picks one for you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can I create a thousand tasks and get a thousand threads?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. Swift uses the cooperative thread pool, a small group of threads that all async work shares.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Too many threads waste memory and slow the app down. The cooperative thread pool avoids that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then I will not block it with long loops. Thanks!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good. Waiting with await is fine, but blocking is not.
